title: Introduce invocation chronicle writer and lightweight SLO explainer
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: Long-tail invocation debugging requires a compact, indexable artifact that can be stored cheaply and joined into dashboards/alerts without pulling full traces. This PR implements a compact 'invocation chronicle' writer that emits fixed-shape invocation snapshots and an asynchronous 'deferred KV joiner' that attaches cached context keys to the chronicle on ingestion. It also ships a lightweight SLO explainer panel for Redwood Console that surfaces cohort-level drivers for SLO misses and an alert weight vector to reduce noisy, repeated alerts. Changes are optimized for low-cardinality metrics and backwards-compatible telemetry fields. Checklist: - [x] Chronicle writer and schema (compact protobuf + JSON fallback) - [x] Deferred KV joiner service that rehydrates chronicle entries asynchronously - [x] Console panel and dashboard widgets for cohort explanations - [x] Sampling policy to avoid high-cardinality explosion - [x] Integration tests for end-to-end ingestion -> dashboard render - [x] Migration docs and observability playbook entry Implementation notes: chronicle entries are capped at ~1.5KB when serialized, prioritized fields: invocation_id, tenant_id (hashed), model_variant, token_counts (input/output), kv_keys_present (list of short hashes), phase_durations (tokenization, model, streaming), error_flags. Deferred KV joiner uses trace_id -> chronicle_id mapping and joins using a low-latency ingest path; failures are retried with exponential backoff and rate-limited per-tenant. The SLO explainer derives three signals per cohort: latency delta (p95 vs baseline), token-cost deviation, and KV cache effectiveness; these feed into an alert weight vector that reduces alert noise by suppressing alerts with low combined weight. Backwards compatibility: new chronicle stream is optional; we default-disabled the console panel via feature flag. Security/PII: tenant_id is hashed, raw prompts are never stored; KV keys are hashed and truncated. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global with monitoring on ingestion error-rate and chronicle size distribution. Related work: replaces ad-hoc per-tenant snapshot hack from ENG-2911. Impact: low runtime overhead in hot path (writer is async buffered), modest storage increase for telemetry, substantial reduction in time-to-debug for long-tail incidents.
